problem.statement: Store emoji and other supplementary-plane characters in a MySQL column using the charset named utf8.

approach.summary: Insert 4-byte UTF-8 characters (emoji) into a column declared with MySQL charset utf8.

failure.point: MySQL utf8 is an alias for utf8mb3 (max 3 bytes per character); 4-byte characters are rejected or truncated with "Incorrect string value" errors.
failure.evidence: MySQL reference manual documents utf8mb3 as a 3-byte-max encoding and directs users to utf8mb4 for full Unicode support.

transferability.notes: Applies wherever the column charset is utf8mb3. Fix (utf8mb4) is universal; MySQL 8 deprecates utf8mb3.
